title: Fake Tech Support
goal: Trick the user into downloading remote access software

script_skeleton.speaker: scammer
script_skeleton.sample: Hello, this is Microsoft Support. We have detected malicious hacking activity on your computer. Your bank details are at risk.

user_options.text: Oh no, what should I do?
user_options.feedback: The scammer wants you to panic. Let's see what they ask for next.

user_options.text: I don't even own a Windows computer.
user_options.feedback: Great catch! Scammers often guess which devices you use.
Perfect! Microsoft will never call you directly to say your computer is hacked.

script_skeleton.speaker: scammer
script_skeleton.sample: I need to secure your network immediately. Please download the 'AnyDesk' app on your phone so I can block the hackers.

user_options.text: Okay, I am downloading it now.
user_options.feedback: Never download screen-sharing apps like AnyDesk on a cold call. This lets the scammer control your phone.

user_options.text: I will take my computer to a local repair shop instead.
user_options.feedback: Excellent choice. Always rely on trusted local professionals rather than strangers on the phone.
Well done! Any request to download remote access software is an immediate red flag.

red_flags: Creating panic about hackers or bank details
Asking you to download apps like AnyDesk or TeamViewer
debrief_success: Great job! Tech companies will never call you out of the blue to warn you about hackers. By hanging up, you kept your device safe.
debrief_failure: If you download remote access software, the scammer can see your screen, read your OTPs, and steal money from your banking apps. Never install apps instructed by a stranger on the phone.
